title: 2026 regional budget and police capital funding
subtitle: Transit changes, seniors' free-fare pilot, women's warming centre, development fees and reserve transfers also considered.
overview: The Strategic Planning and Budget Committee spent the day on the 2026 Plan and Budget and recommended it to Council {{vote:m54}}. As amended, the operating budget has a net expenditure of $1,801,533,210 and a property tax levy of $887,328,641. Final approval rests with Council.

On policing, the committee recommended the Waterloo Regional Police Service operating budget {{vote:m3}} and its capital budget {{vote:m4}}. A motion to send the capital budget back for a smaller version failed on a tie {{vote:m2}}. Other recommended changes include removing GRT fare inspectors from buses, a six-month free-transit pilot for seniors, funding for a women's overnight warming centre in Cambridge, and a freeze on regional planning fees at 2025 levels while staff develop a new fee framework.

To limit the tax increase, the committee recommended moving money out of several reserves {{vote:m32}}. Motions to restore frequent service on GRT routes 9, 13, 19 and 30 {{vote:m10}} and to defer several capital projects were defeated. The committee deferred a proposed hospital levy to May 2026 {{vote:m43}}. The minutes record no report from the closed session on a labour relations matter.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended Council approve the 2026 Plan, operating budget and capital budget as amended, with a levy of $887,328,641 {{vote:m54}}.
The committee recommended approving the Waterloo Regional Police Service 2026 capital budget and 2027-2035 forecast {{vote:m4}}, after a motion to send it back for reduction failed.
The committee recommended removing the proposed expansion of fare inspectors onto GRT buses from the 2026 budget, with staffing, revenue and expenses adjusted {{vote:m5}}.
The committee recommended a pilot of free GRT transit one day a week for residents 65 and older, for at least six months, using GRT App Pay so data can be analysed {{vote:m8}}.
The committee recommended including $176,000 in 2026 to launch a 20-bed women's overnight warming centre in Cambridge, rising to $440,000 in the 2027 base budget {{vote:m22}}.
The committee recommended freezing planning and development fees at 2025 levels and asked staff to bring back a tiered fee framework and a discretionary fee-waiver mechanism {{vote:m25}}.
The committee recommended transferring $1,233,000 from four reserves to the Tax Stabilization Reserve Fund, to reduce the 2026 tax rate by at least $500,000 {{vote:m32}}.
The committee recommended reinstating free delivery of taxi coupons and keeping the price at $30 per $60 value, funded from the accessibility reserve {{vote:m13}}.

debate: On the police communications centre, supporters said the current centre dates from 1992, police facilities have no room to grow, and the building is meant for long-term growth and technology. Critics called it oversized, questioned its cost per square foot, and noted no partner agencies had committed. They also pointed to the region's debt load and competing priorities.

On the seniors' free-transit pilot, staff warned of lost revenue and said operators do not check ID, so the pilot needed a payment app or card to collect any data. Supporters said it could reduce isolation and bring new riders, and the app requirement was added.

On development fees, supporters said some regional fees were close to or above what area municipalities charge for far more work. Staff said the 2025 fee schedule did not reflect the region's current commenting role or actual costs, and agreed a waiver mechanism would help.

On the reserve transfers and tax stabilization, staff cautioned that reserves were below target and that the strategic plan and museum reserves needed their funding. One councillor argued for using reserves to lower the levy. The museum transfer and a strategic plan transfer were later removed or replaced.

Several motions to cut capital or expense lines failed. Staff said the lines covered building systems, accessibility work and contracts that were hard to reduce, while the mover said the region needed to hold down costs for residents.
